title: The Math That Doubles Prices While You Sleep

beats.say: The price of almost everything doubles while you sleep, slowly.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of worn keys resting on a dark, rain-slicked concrete ledge under a single sodium streetlamp, low angle.

beats.say: You check your grocery receipt and wonder why a simple cart of food costs way more than it did last year.
beats.visual: High angle shot of a solitary shopping cart abandoned in a massive, empty asphalt parking lot at blue hour.

beats.say: How fast does inflation actually steal your purchasing power behind your back?
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a lone commuter walking down a massive concrete underpass, wet asphalt reflecting cold fluorescent light.

beats.say: Most people assume a stable three percent inflation rate is harmless and barely changes your daily life.
beats.visual: Cinematic shot of a heavy steel bridge tower edge cutting into thick fog under a grey overcast sky.

beats.say: Here's what the math actually says. At three percent inflation, prices double in twenty four years.
beats.visual: Low angle of a heavy metal railway crossing arm resting against a dim evening sky, no text.

beats.say: Look at $100 today. After twenty years of three percent inflation, it's worth just $55 in buying power.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of worn leather wallet edges on a dark wood table under a single practical light, shadows stretching far.

beats.say: Why does that invisible shrinkage happen so fast to money you worked hard to earn?
beats.visual: A tiny human silhouette walking past a towering brutalist concrete wall, natural fog rolling in from the side.

beats.say: It happens because of the Rule of Seventy-Two. Divide seventy-two by three, and you get twenty-four years.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a rusty mechanical gear mechanism turning slowly in deep shadow, cold blue light glinting on steel.

beats.say: That's the exact timeline for your dollar to lose half its real weight.
beats.visual: Wide shot of empty highway lanes stretching into a dark horizon under a heavy, overcast sodium light.

beats.say: To beat that silent erosion, your cash has to work harder than you do.
beats.visual: Low angle view of a massive stone bridge pylon rising straight up into a dark, foggy sky.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Extreme close of a heavy brass door latch resting in deep shadow, single practical light beam cutting across.
